children: Barnes & Noble Education reported fiscal 2027 first-quarter revenue of $290.6 million and a narrowed net loss of $12.9 million for the 13 weeks ended August 1, 2026. Adjusted EBITDA improved to a loss of $9.3 million, a year-over-year improvement of $2.2 million. The company reiterated full-year fiscal 2027 guidance, targeting Adjusted EBITDA of $85 million to $92 million.
Revenue: $290.6 million for the quarter ended August 1, 2026, up $2.4 million or 0.8% year-over-year.
Net loss: $(12.9) million for the quarter, a 29.3% improvement from a $(18.3) million loss in the prior-year period.
Adjusted EBITDA: $(9.3) million for the quarter, improved $2.2 million (18.9%) versus $(11.5) million in the prior-year period.
Total debt: $123.5 million at quarter end, down from $170.0 million a year earlier.
Working capital: $236.8 million of positive working capital at the end of the quarter.
BNC First Day programs revenue increased by $10.3 million, or 9.0%, to $124.7 million year-over-year, driving a primary portion of revenue growth.
Gross comparable store sales rose $10.7 million, or 3.7%, year-over-year; revenue growth was partially offset by store closures and exits from less profitable locations.

First Day Complete expansion: offered across 263 campuses for Fall 2026, reaching more than 1.43 million students—approximately 26% growth versus Fall 2025 (student counts per NCES data as of Jan 2, 2026).
Declared and paid a quarterly dividend of $0.08 per share (paid July 30, 2026 to shareholders of record July 16, 2026).

Company emphasized continued focus on operating leverage, disciplined expense management, capital efficiency and reductions in debt and interest expense; projected ~ $20 million in capital expenditures for fiscal 2027.
